 That's all the Cleveland Guardians needed to make it to the World Series for the first time in a decade. Unfortunately, the Guardians dropped three consecutive games to the Tampa Bay Rays and were eliminated in the ALCS.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Since Cleveland last played in the Fall Classic, the team has undergone a handful of changes, including trades and a limited number of free-agent signings.
 The Guardians organization has long been known for savvy, strategic transactions that have kept them in playoff contention for over a decade.
 It always feels like Cleveland ends up on the winning side of their trades with other teams.
 However, that hasn't always been the case, and the World Series matchup between the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays is a painful reminder of what the current Guardians team is missing out on.
 The group of players the Guardians will get to watch play in the World Series includes Junior Caminero, Yandy Diaz, Richie Palacios, and Jake Bauers. Okay, fine, Kevin Kelly counts, too.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Something that all four of these players have in common is that they were all part of Cleveland's organization at one point or another. In the case of Yandy Diaz and Jake Bauers, who were actually traded for one another, they even spent extended stretches with the big-league team.
 Oct 17, 2026; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Tampa Bay Rays infielder Junior Caminero (13) reacts at second base after hitting an RBI double and Cleveland Guardians infielder Travis Bazzana (37) looks on during the sixth inning in game four of the ALCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Progressive Field. Mandatory Credit: David Dermer-Imagn Images
 Cleveland signed Diaz to a Minor League contract in the fall of 2013. Four years later, in April 2017, he made his MLB debut with the then-Indians. Diaz spent the next two years with Cleveland, slugging .283/.361/.366 in 88 games.
 Following the 2018 season, Cleveland didn't see a future fit with Diaz on the roster and traded him to Tampa Bay for prized prospect Jake Bauers.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement It just so happens Bauers is also playing in the World Series, just not with the Guardians.
 Bauers' two-year stint in Cleveland was disappointing, to say the least. He only had a .656 OPS with the team in two years, and the front office decided to part ways in 2019. Bauers then bounced between five minor league teams and played for the Seattle Mariners and New York Yankees before finding a home with the Brewers.
 The 2026 campaign was Bauer' best season as a big-league player, logging a .874 OPS, including 26 home runs. He was even named NLCS MVP after two series-defining home runs against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
 Bauers admitted he was ready to walk away from baseball, but came back simply for health care after his daughter was born.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement While Cleveland decided whether it was time to go in a different direction with the return from the Diaz trade, another storyline was developing in the background.
 In the summer of 2019, Cleveland signed a 17-year-old infielder to a minor league deal. His name was Junior Caminero. Just over two years later, Cleveland traded him to the Rays, and the rest is history.
 Caminero has become one of baseball's top young stars. The 23-year-old debuted in 2023 and owns a .844 OPS with 94 home runs in his first four big-league seasons. His power from the right side of the plate is unmatched, and some of the current Guardians team would love to have him.
 Every organization has moves it wishes it could go back and change. Unfortunately, three transactions Cleveland was on the wrong end of are key to their teams in the Fall Classic.
 Now, the Guardians are left to wonder what could have been if Bauers, Caminero, Diaz, or even Palacios were still on the roster.
